hypothesis: Batching seven common renderer variants with two virtualized FULL controls could amortize one renderer import process.
scope: one action for seven shared standard renderer variants plus VM and Firecracker FULL controls; MCP fixture remains separate

baseline.overlap: all seven standard actions began within about 73ms; last action ended about 30.048s after first action start; do not sum their wall durations

candidate.same_invocation_caveat: successful TestRunner used the batch action output from the earlier physical candidate run; do not call that invocation a matched cold whole-graph comparison

comparison.render_action_cpu: baseline seven actions total 219.212 CPU seconds versus candidate batch action 38.620124 CPU seconds, a 180.592 CPU-second reduction across these render actions; this is an aggregate CPU benefit, not observed wall-time or queue saving
comparison.render_wall: candidate batch 30.940s versus baseline slowest standard render 30.031s; all baseline renders overlapped, so batching shows no wall-time benefit and adds about 0.91s to the renderer critical path in this observed pair
comparison.test_runner_wall: candidate 28.455s versus baseline 26.300445s, about 2.155s slower; test-runner CPU is nearly unchanged
comparison.selective_consumer: k3s/defs.bzl selects the VM profile by its individual rendered JSON path; under the candidate that file is an output of the nine-output batch, so a VM-only consumer would materialize unrelated profiles. VM standalone baseline action was 27.009s/31.155 CPU; no matched VM-only action measurement on the candidate was run.
comparison.decision_scope: reject this seven-shared-variant plus two-FULL-controls batching arrangement for CI latency; revisit if measured renderer CPU capacity or CPU queueing becomes a limiting factor

output_equivalence.method: compare candidate CAS digests from the batch ActionResult with baseline render ActionResults
output_equivalence.unverified_standard_profile: central-budget: baseline action result lookup returned NotFound, so exact digest comparison could not be completed
output_equivalence.full_controls: No baseline declared-file CAS digests existed for VM/Firecracker FULL outputs; preserved profile-equivalence testcases passed in candidate JUnit using the same FULL defaults and arguments.

revisit_trigger: Revisit only if measured renderer CPU contention or CPU queueing is limiting a selected CI critical path; this experiment shows aggregate CPU reduction but no burst, queue, or complete-feedback saving.
limits: The seven baseline standard actions overlapped substantially; their wall durations are not additive.
The candidate successful TestRunner consumed the batch action output from an earlier physical render action, so there was no matched cold whole-graph comparison.
The candidate batch also generated two FULL controls absent as separate declared baseline outputs.

Six of seven standard output CAS digests match; central-budget baseline result was unavailable. The two FULL controls were covered by passing equivalence assertions but have no baseline declared-file digest.
No source optimization was adopted and no CI gate or policy changed.
